title: US officials tell House hearing the string of November outages was not a cyberattack
date_note: Date of the House Homeland Security hearing (18 Nov) per The Record; the outages Hankook Ilbo lists run 12 to 17 November.
summary: Hankook Ilbo lists outages from 12 to 17 November at Outlook and Teams, an FAA communications system, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple and an NSA network. At a House Homeland Security hearing, The Record reports, FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia said there was "no indication whatsoever" of malicious cyber activity and DNI Jay Clayton said it was "not an orchestrated attack by a foreign malign actor". EFE reports Trump called them independent events.
plain: US security officials told Congress that a run of outages at several big services was not caused by a cyberattack, news reports say.
exec: Officials quoted by the sources say the outages at major US services were not a coordinated or malicious cyberattack.
impact: Outages named by the article: Outlook and Teams, FAA communications, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple services, an NSA internal network.

validation.note: The Record (18 Nov, hearing coverage), Hankook Ilbo and AZ Free News each report officials saying there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack; El Financiero (EFE, 20 Nov) reports Trump calling them independent events. Hearing transcript not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, outage list, Clayton and Trump quotes against Hankook Ilbo, AZ Free News, El Financiero; they hold. exec carried rushed-patching and former-analyst claims not in summary; rewritten to restate the summary.
